items.title: Nvidia, Apple, Broadcom in 'fierce' battle to make chips at TSMC
items.author: Katie Tarasov
items.highlights: As Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co.'s Add To Watchlist record quarter makes clear, demand from chipmakers shows no sign of slowing down. In fact, TSMC can't manufacture quickly enough. The artificial intelligence boom has created unending need for space on factory lines at the world's leading chip manufacturer, and it could put a chokehold on the entire industry's ability to scale. Last year, TSMC said it had the capacity to make more than 17 million 12-inch equivalent wafers. But customers want more. items.title: Can robust TSMC earnings help settle AI jitters? By Investing.com
items.author: Senad Karaahmetovic
items.highlights: Investing.com - TSMC posted a $23.59 billion net profit for the third quarter of 2026, a 68.7% year-over-year surge that marked its sixth consecutive record quarter, yet the earnings beat has done little to arrest a deepening selloff across AI-linked semiconductor stocks. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing, the world’s largest contract chipmaker and a foundry supplier to NVIDIA, AMD, and Apple, is the stock most exposed to AI hardware demand: its revenue is tied directly to the volume and complexity of chips ordered by hyperscalers and AI accelerator makers.
